clinicalPearls: A focal, task-specific laryngeal dystonia in which involuntary spasms of the intrinsic laryngeal muscles disrupt voice during speech but spare other laryngeal functions
The adductor type is most common, producing a strained, strangled, effortful voice with abrupt voice breaks on vowels
The abductor type produces breathy breaks and aphonic whispered segments, especially on voiceless consonants
Symptoms are task-specific: the voice may be normal during whispering, singing, laughing, or crying but abnormal during connected speech
It is frequently accompanied by voice tremor and may coexist with other focal dystonias
Diagnosis is clinical, supported by perceptual voice assessment and flexible laryngoscopy showing task-specific spasms with a structurally normal larynx
Botulinum toxin injection into the affected laryngeal muscles is the mainstay of treatment, giving temporary relief that requires periodic repetition
reference.pathophysiology: Spasmodic dysphonia is a focal task-specific dystonia of the larynx, considered a disorder of central motor control within the basal ganglia and their cortical and brainstem connections rather than a structural or purely psychogenic problem. Abnormal, involuntary co-contraction of the laryngeal muscles occurs selectively during the fine motor task of speech. In the adductor form the vocal folds press together excessively, interrupting phonation with strained breaks; in the abductor form inappropriate opening produces breathy, aphonic breaks. The larynx is structurally normal and the dystonia typically does not affect breathing or swallowing.
additionalDifferentials: Vocal tremor (essential tremor of the voice)
additionalInvestigations: Flexible fibreoptic laryngoscopy and stroboscopy during connected speech and other vocal tasks
Perceptual and acoustic voice analysis by a speech and language therapist
Laryngeal electromyography in selected or atypical cases
Neurological examination for other focal dystonias or tremor
MRI of the brain if an atypical or secondary dystonia is suspected
Trial of botulinum toxin as both a therapeutic and confirmatory measure
redFlags: Associated stridor or airway compromise suggesting a different or additional laryngeal disorder
Progressive generalised neurological signs suggesting a wider neurodegenerative process
A structural vocal fold lesion on endoscopy
Rapid onset after a clear psychological precipitant suggesting a functional disorder
reference.prognosis: Spasmodic dysphonia is a chronic condition without spontaneous cure, but botulinum toxin injections reliably improve the voice for several months at a time, and combined botulinum toxin and voice therapy allow most patients to maintain functional communication.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosing it as muscle tension or psychogenic dysphonia and delaying appropriate treatment
Failing to assess the voice across multiple tasks to reveal its task-specific nature
Overlooking coexisting vocal tremor, which affects treatment response
Confusing abductor spasmodic dysphonia with vocal fold paresis
Attributing all voice breaks to reflux or structural lesions
